name: Formulae, equations and amounts of substance

terms.definition: The number of particles in one mole of a substance.
terms.examiner: 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹, from the Data Booklet. Say what the particles are: atoms, molecules, ions or electrons.

terms.definition: The mass of one mole of a substance, in g mol⁻¹.
terms.examiner: Amount in moles = mass ÷ molar mass.

terms.definition: The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound.
The actual number of atoms of each element in a molecule of a compound.
terms.examiner: It is a whole-number multiple of the empirical formula; use the molar mass to find the multiple.

terms.definition: The volume occupied by one mole of any gas: 24 dm³ mol⁻¹ at room temperature and pressure.
terms.examiner: The value is in the Data Booklet. Convert cm³ to dm³ first.

terms.definition: pV = nRT, with pressure in Pa, volume in m³ and temperature in K.
terms.examiner: Most marks are lost on units: cm³ to m³ is × 10⁻⁶, dm³ to m³ is × 10⁻³, kPa to Pa is × 1000.

terms.definition: (Molar mass of the desired product ÷ sum of the molar masses of all products) × 100.
terms.examiner: Use the balanced equation, so include the numbers in front of each formula.

terms.definition: (Actual amount of product ÷ theoretical maximum amount of product) × 100.
terms.examiner: Work in moles or in mass, but the same for both.

terms.definition: Titres that agree closely with each other.
terms.examiner: Only concordant titres go into the mean; leave out the rough titre.
